results.summary_before: This project recreates the classic Mastermind game where players guess a secret combination of colors. It uses a random number generator to set the secret code and compares guesses to provide feedback on correct and half-correct positions. The game supports up to 16 turns and outputs hints via pins intended for seven-segment displays. It is a simple VHDL implementation of a puzzle game, best experienced with external displays.

results.summary_before: This Wokwi project combines a simple snake game (TinySnake) with a design called PRISM, though the documentation does not describe what PRISM does. The snake game speed is controlled by the eight input pins, with larger values producing slower movement, and the game state is shown on a 7-segment display. The design requires only the on-board 7-segment display and no other external hardware. The documentation is thin and lacks details about the PRISM portion and how the two designs interact.
